role: Lead Systems Architect & Full-Stack Engineer (BukSU CMS-V2)
task_description: Resolved three critical structural and visual bugs in Turnitin-style academic integrity highlight overlay: (1) Eliminated matched text string rendering inside highlight elements, enforcing pure geometric translucent rectangles with zero child text; (2) Implemented buildTurnitinHighlightRects baseline clustering in plagiarismHighlightAdapter.js to decompose multi-line passages into discrete line rectangles, eliminating off-canvas right-margin horizontal overflow; (3) Resolved PDF.js textLayer flex and purple highlight bleed by importing pdfjs-dist/web/pdf_viewer.css and enforcing strict CSS overrides (display: block, color: transparent, background-color: transparent); (4) Enforced mixBlendMode: multiply and opacity: 0.28 (0.45 when selected) to preserve 100% canvas text legibility; (5) Anchored source pill badge [N] exclusively to the top-left of the first rectangle in a cluster (index === 0). Verified with 63 unit tests across 6 suites, UNMATCHED_COUNT=0 route parity, and 60/60 agentic validation checks.

verification_evidence.governance_pipeline: 11 agents valid, DAG verified, 0 errors, 0 warnings

lessons_learned: Lesson: PDF highlight overlays must never render text strings ({match.text}) as child elements over canvas; highlights are strictly geometric masks with mixBlendMode: multiply and opacity: 0.28.

Lesson: Matched passages extracted from PDF layout analysis must be clustered into discrete visual line bounding boxes using baseline tolerance clustering to avoid flex-direction row horizontal overflow into margins.

Lesson: react-pdf-highlighter-plus requires pdfjs-dist/web/pdf_viewer.css to be explicitly imported; otherwise .textLayer becomes a flex container and textLayer spans become visible flex items instead of absolutely positioned transparent spans.
